explanations.answer: Evildoers are good in His sight
explanations.explanation: That's the one, friend. The people had been saying, “All who do evil are good in the sight of the LORD, and in them He delights.” The verse calls those words wearying to Him. Think of a guy who keeps telling the same bad story at every gathering, and everybody just nods and checks the clock.

Not in this verse, friend. The words recorded here are, “All who do evil are good in the sight of the LORD, and in them He delights,” and “Where is the God of justice?” Offerings don't come up until later, in 3:3-4. I'd stamp this one on my own forehead, but my hat is too tall for that.

explanations.answer: The prophets don't speak for Him
explanations.explanation: That one isn't in the verse. What the people said is about evildoers: “All who do evil are good in the sight of the LORD, and in them He delights.” Then they add, “Where is the God of justice?” Nothing here is about the prophets. The text keeps it to those two lines, and I'll do the same.
Right on target, baker. The LORD of Hosts says, “Behold, I will send My messenger…” That's the whole promise in one line. Short and clear, like a note taped to the oven door.
No king in this verse, friend. The LORD of Hosts says, “Behold, I will send My messenger…” A messenger carries something to somebody. That's the job, plain and simple.

I get why that sounds big, but the verse doesn't say it. The LORD of Hosts says, “Behold, I will send My messenger…” No sword, no armor, no trumpet. Just a messenger, and what he does comes in the next line.

That's it, baker. The messenger “will prepare the way before Me,” the LORD of Hosts says. Then the Lord the people seek comes to His temple. The messenger goes first and gets things ready, kind of like the one who sets out the cooling racks before the batch comes out.

explanations.answer: Guard the doors of His temple
explanations.explanation: The temple is in the verse, but the guard job isn't. The text says the messenger “will prepare the way before Me.” After that the Lord comes to His temple. Nobody's standing at the door with a clipboard.

No head count here, friend. The messenger's job in this verse is to “prepare the way before Me.” That's what the LORD of Hosts says. I'd happily count cookies all day, but that's my job, not the messenger's.

Yes, friend. The verse says the Lord whom they seek “will suddenly come to His temple.” There's no long warning ahead of the arrival. It's like pulling the drawer open and finding the light already pouring in.
The verse says the opposite, baker. The Lord whom they seek “will suddenly come to His temple.” The word is suddenly. Nobody gets a long runway to tidy up first.

You got it, baker. The LORD of Hosts calls Him “the Messenger of the covenant, in whom you delight.” The people delight in Him, and then comes “see, He is coming.” That's good news aimed straight at them.
Look again at the verse, friend. The LORD of Hosts calls Him “the Messenger of the covenant, in whom you delight.” So it's true, not false. Delight is the exact word the text uses.

explanations.answer: He'll be like a refiner's fire
explanations.explanation: That's the one, baker. The verse says, “For He will be like a refiner's fire, like a launderer's soap.” Fire and soap are no small things. That's why the question is, “Who can stand when He appears?”

explanations.answer: He'll come with a great army
explanations.explanation: No army in this verse, friend. The reason given is, “For He will be like a refiner's fire, like a launderer's soap.” The picture is a workshop kind of picture, not a battlefield. It's still serious enough that the people are asked who can stand.

explanations.answer: He'll shake the earth and sky
explanations.explanation: That's not what the verse says, friend. It says, “For He will be like a refiner's fire, like a launderer's soap.” The text gives fire and soap, not quakes and skies. Stick to what's in the verse and it'll steer you right.
Levi it is, baker. The verse says, “He will purify the sons of Levi and refine them like gold and silver.” Gold and silver are the picture here. The refiner sits down and takes his time with it.

Benjamin isn't named in the verse, friend. The text says the Lord “will purify the sons of Levi and refine them like gold and silver.” Levi is the name that fits the blank. Next time the name will be waiting for you.
Close to the right neighborhood, but no. Ephraim isn't named in this verse. It says, “He will purify the sons of Levi and refine them like gold and silver.” Levi is the one that fills the blank.
Yes, baker. The verse says, “Then they will present offerings to the LORD in righteousness.” The refining comes first, and the offerings follow. Clean tools make clean cookies, and I would know.
The verse says it plainly, friend. After the refining, “Then they will present offerings to the LORD in righteousness.” So the statement is true. The word that sticks is righteousness.

Please is the word, baker. The verse says, “Then the offerings of Judah and Jerusalem will please the LORD, as in days of old and years gone by.” It looks back to earlier days. Good news, and I'm smiling about it.

Not this time, friend. The verse says the offerings of Judah and Jerusalem “will please the LORD, as in days of old and years gone by.” The refining leads to something good. The word that fits the blank is please.

That's not the word, friend. The verse says the offerings of Judah and Jerusalem “will please the LORD, as in days of old and years gone by.” After the refining, the tone turns glad. Please is the one that fits.

The word in the verse is the opposite of slow, friend. The LORD of Hosts says, “And I will be a swift witness against sorcerers and adulterers and perjurers…” Swift, not slow. So the statement is false, and the verse settles it.

Right, baker. The LORD of Hosts says, “And I will be a swift witness against sorcerers and adulterers and perjurers…” The word is swift, so slow doesn't fit. Reading the verse carefully pays off, like checking the timer before the batch.

explanations.answer: Those who cheat workers of their wages
explanations.explanation: That's on the list, baker. The LORD of Hosts says He will be a witness “against those who defraud laborers of their wages.” Think of a boss who keeps promising the paycheck is coming. It's right there next to the oppressors of the widowed and fatherless.

explanations.answer: Those who skip the yearly feasts
explanations.explanation: That one isn't on His list, friend. The LORD names sorcerers, adulterers, perjurers, those who oppress the widowed and fatherless, those who “defraud laborers of their wages,” and those who deny justice to the foreigner. Yearly feasts don't appear. Wages do.

explanations.answer: Those who eat food that is unclean
explanations.explanation: Not on this list, friend. The LORD names sorcerers, adulterers, perjurers, oppressors of the widowed and fatherless, those who “defraud laborers of their wages,” and those who deny justice to the foreigner. Food isn't mentioned. The right answer is the one about cheating workers.

Fear is the word, baker. The list ends with those who “deny justice to the foreigner but do not fear Me,” says the LORD of Hosts. It's the last item, and the LORD's own words put it there. That's a heavy line, so let's let it sit for a moment.

Not this one, friend. The verse says, “…deny justice to the foreigner but do not fear Me,” says the LORD of Hosts. The word is fear. It's a heavy ending to the list, so I'll keep my jokes in the oven.
That's not the word, friend. The verse says, “…deny justice to the foreigner but do not fear Me,” says the LORD of Hosts. The blank holds fear. It's the closing line of a serious list.
